raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both papers have complete, readable full texts and originate from the same research group (Governance and Sustainability Lab, Trier University) under the BMBF-funded WaterPower project (grant 01 LN 1316 A) in the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area (GAMA), with Study B citing Study A as reference [13]. Despite sharing the broader research programme and an initial August–November 2015 fieldwork window, their primary empirical samples, geographies, respondent groups, and analytical designs are distinct. Study A examines household-level land and domestic water access and customary land/local water control in two specific peri-urban localities (Oduman and Pantang; August–November 2015), drawing on 62 household interviews (which included 25 local/neighbourhood water providers), 17 interviews with traditional authorities, elders, youth-group members, and landowner associations, 4 household photo diaries, transect walks, and background institutional expert interviews. Study B (led by R. Alba, who conducted the field investigation across August–November 2015 and August–September 2017) examines urban water governance and mobile tanker brokerage across urban and peri-urban Accra, drawing on 12 days of ride-along participant observation and interviews with tanker truck drivers, mates, and truck owners across four tanker associations (primarily urban North-West and East Accra/Adenta plus one peri-urban association) alongside 15 in-depth interviews with municipal, GWCL, PURC, MWRWH Water Directorate, and World Bank officials. At most, some background water-sector expert interviews in late 2015 may have been conducted jointly by the project team (used only as institutional context in Study A, where only a Stool Lands official is cited, versus formal governance analysis in Study B), so double-counting risk in synthesis is low.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Qualitative case study in two peri-urban localities of the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area (GAMA), Ghana—Oduman (Ga West Municipality) and Pantang (La Nkwantanang-Madina Municipality)—conducted between August and November 2015 under the BMBF WaterPower project. Data include 62 semi-structured household interviews across original villages (n = 13) and new settlement sites (n = 49) encompassing 25 local private water providers, plus interviews with traditional authorities (3), elders (9), youth organisation members (3), and landowner associations (2), supplemented by transect walks, 1-week photo diaries in 4 households, and background expert interviews on land/water institutional setup.
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Practice-based ethnographic and qualitative governance study of mobile tanker water supply across urban and peri-urban Accra (GAMA), Ghana, conducted between August and November 2015 and August to September 2017 under the BMBF WaterPower project. Data include 12 days of ride-along participant observation, mapping, semi-structured interviews, and informal conversations by the first author (R. Alba) with tanker truck drivers, truck owners, and mates across four organized tanker associations (three urban in North-West and East Accra/Adenta, one peri-urban) plus individual drivers, together with 15 in-depth interviews with municipal officials, GWCL engineers and field staff, PURC members, MWRWH Water Directorate officials, and World Bank staff.
